context:
Patient: 59F, breast cancer survivor (2016: dose-dense AC, cumulative doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left breast RT, on anastrozole), presents with left axillary mass, fevers to 38.4 C, drenching night sweats; ECOG 1, LDH 510. Non-GCB DLBCL (MYC 45%, BCL2 70%, FISH negative for rearrangements), PET nodes above and below the diaphragm plus splenic nodules, marrow negative, and new LVEF 45% (62% in 2016) with GLS -14%.
What this case tests: Spleen is a nodal site under Lugano, so stage is III, not IV, and IPI is 2. | Double-expressor by IHC but FISH-negative, so not double-hit; no intensification to DA-EPOCH-R. | Prior doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left chest RT and LVEF 62% to 45% mean standard full-dose R-CHOP / Pola-R-CHP is not safe as is. | Treatment must stay curative: anthracycline-free (R-CEOP / R-GCVP) or cardio-protected regimen, with cardio-oncology input and cardioprotective drugs. | CNS-IPI 2 with no high-risk sites: no routine CNS prophylaxis.

answer.diagnosis: Newly diagnosed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, NOS (SNOMED 109969005; ICD-10-CM C83.30), diagnosed on excisional biopsy of a left axillary lymph node performed 2026-08-25 (pathology 2026-08-28, amended 2026-09-08 with FISH). This is a de novo non-Hodgkin lymphoma, NOT a recurrence, metastasis or nodal metastasis of her 2016 left breast carcinoma: the tumor is CD20/PAX5 positive with a clonal kappa-restricted large B-cell population on flow cytometry, cytokeratin AE1/AE3 and GATA3 are negative in lesional cells, there is no cohesive epithelial nesting or single-file infiltration, the left breast has no FDG-avid lesion on PET-CT and its 2026-03-02 mammogram was BI-RADS 2 (post-treatment). It is also not therapy-related to her 2016 doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide: the interval is 10 years (outside the 5-7 year window for alkylator-related secondary AML/MDS), there are no cytopenias, no marrow dysplasia and no clonal cytogenetics. The diagnosis is confirmed and adequate to begin therapy; no additional biopsy is required for diagnosis, and I do not need to biopsy the 7.5 cm mesenteric conglomerate (same FDG pattern as the biopsy-proven axillary disease).
answer.stage: Ann Arbor / Lugano stage III with splenic involvement and B symptoms (stage IIIB-S). Nodal disease both above the diaphragm (left axillary nodes, largest 2.2 cm, SUVmax 17.8; mediastinal prevascular and left paratracheal nodes, largest 2.9 cm, SUVmax 15.4) and below the diaphragm (mesenteric nodal conglomerate 7.5 x 5.1 cm, SUVmax 22.3; para-aortic nodes up to 3.0 cm, SUVmax 16.9), plus multiple FDG-avid splenic nodules (spleen 12.8 cm, nodules up to 2.1 cm, SUVmax 16.2); spleen counts as an extranodal (S) site. Bone marrow (right posterior iliac crest, 2026-09-08) is negative by morphology, CD20/PAX5 immunostains and flow cytometry. No CNS, breast, testicular, liver, lung, bone, adrenal, renal or peritoneal disease and no effusion. Largest mass 7.5 cm = high-volume disease but NOT bulky by Lugano criteria (bulky = >=10 cm). B symptoms present: recurrent unexplained evening fever to 38.4 C and drenching night sweats 2-3 times weekly for ~5 weeks; the third Lugano B criterion (weight loss >10% in 6 months) is not met (72.8 kg in March 2026 to 70.1 kg on 2026-09-17, about 3.7%). ECOG 1. Hgb 11.4 g/dL (not <10 g/dL) and platelets 178 K/uL, so no Ann Arbor stage-IV cytopenia criteria are met. Baseline labs otherwise preserved: Cr 0.8, eGFR 85, Na 139, K 4.2, Ca 9.3, albumin 3.8, AST 24, ALT 22, ALP 92, total bilirubin 0.6, urate 5.8.
answer.biology: DLBCL, NOS (WHO-HAEM5 / ICC 2022): CD20 positive (diffuse, strong), PAX5 positive, CD3 negative in tumor, CD5 negative, CD10 negative, BCL6 positive, MUM1/IRF4 positive (~80%), BCL2 positive (~70%), MYC positive (~45%), cyclin D1 negative, CD30 negative, Ki-67 ~80%, EBER-ISH negative; flow cytometry CD19+/CD20+/CD10- with kappa light-chain restricted large B-cell population (62% of events). Cell of origin by Hans is non-germinal-center (ABC-like), an adverse prognostic feature. FISH on 200 nuclei (2026-09-08) shows NO MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement, so this is NOT high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements (double-hit) and not triple-hit; the favorable FISH results substantially reduce the concern for double-hit biology and remove the indication for double-hit-directed therapy. By IHC she is a BORDERLINE double expressor (MYC 45%, BCL2 70%, using the >=40% and >=50% thresholds; MYC sits below the stricter 50% cut-off, and BCL2 expression is common in non-GCB/ABC DLBCL without rearrangement, so the independent prognostic weight of the double-expressor designation in this subtype is uncertain). Other biology: no EBV-driven disease (EBER-); no MYD88, BCL2/IGH or CCND1 rearrangement reported; CD30 negative, so brentuximab vedotin is not applicable; CD20 positive, so anti-CD20 therapy is appropriate; no transformation from a indolent lymphoma identified.
answer.prognosis: Intermediate-high risk by NCCN B-Cell Lymphomas. IPI = 3 (age <60 = 0, stage III-IV = 1, LDH 510 elevated = 1, ECOG 1 = 1, <=1 extranodal site = 0) = high-intermediate risk. NCCN-IPI = 3 (age >=60 0, LDH elevated 1, stage III-IV 1, ECOG >=1 1, >1 extranodal site 0) = high-intermediate risk. CNS-IPI = 3 (LDH elevated 1, ECOG 1 = 1, stage III-IV = 1; age <60 0, eGFR 85 0, albumin 3.8 0, extranodal sites <=1 0) = intermediate CNS risk. Adverse features: non-GCB/ABC subtype, borderline double-expressor immunophenotype, Ki-67 ~80%, LDH roughly 2x upper limit of normal (510 vs 182 in March 2026), B symptoms, bulky-adjacent/high-volume disease (largest mass 7.5 cm, SUVmax 22) and splenic involvement. Favorable features: ECOG 1, age 59, no Lugano bulky disease, no bone marrow, CNS, breast or testicular involvement, no diabetes, no neutropenia, normal renal and hepatic function, no prior autologous transplant, and a preserved baseline LVEF without HF symptoms (NYHA I) despite reduced EF. Overall expectation: 5-year OS and cure probability of roughly 55-60% with rituximab-based chemoimmunotherapy for IPI 3 DLBCL (a competing cardiac mortality risk from her newly reduced LVEF and prior chest radiotherapy adds to the non-cancer mortality estimate); I would not quote better than this given the ABC/non-GCB subtype and elevated LDH. A Deauville 4-5 interim PET after 3 cycles would lower the expected cure to roughly 30-40%, and any IPI contribution from the borderline double-expressor phenotype could shave a further few percent. She is NOT in the highest-risk group (no double-hit, no bulky disease, no marrow/CNS disease, ECOG 1), so I expect her to be cured with standard-duration first-line therapy plus consolidation only if she relapses.
answer.first_line_treatment: DECISION: begin first-line systemic therapy in late September/early October 2026 with POLATUZUMAB VEDOTIN + R-CHP (no anthracycline) for 6 cycles (21-day cycles): polatuzumab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV (about 126 mg) day 1, rituximab 375 mg/m2 (about 671 mg) day 1, cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 (about 1,342 mg) day 1, vincristine 1.4 mg/m2 capped at 2 mg day 1, prednisone 100 mg days 1-5, every 21 days x 6 cycles, with pegfilgrastim 6 mg SC on day 9 of every cycle; polatuzumab monotherapy for up to 2 additional cycles (7 and 8) at my discretion after a complete metabolic response, per the POLARIX schedule. Key reasons for this choice: (1) CARDIAC SAFETY - she has received 240 mg/m2 of doxorubicin in 2016 with left breast tangential radiotherapy, and her LVEF has fallen from 62% (2016) to 45% with global longitudinal strain -14% (2026-09-09), so a further 300 mg/m2 of doxorubicin would take her to 540 mg/m2 total in a patient who has already developed LV dysfunction; omitting anthracycline removes the largest modifiable cardiotoxicity risk in a woman who is explicitly worried about her heart and whose mother died of heart failure, without compromising cure probability in her risk group; (2) EFFICACY - POLARIX (in untreated DLBCL with IPI 2-5, which includes her IPI 3) showed superior PFS versus R-CHOP (24-month EFS 81.9% vs 70.2%) and a favorable OS signal that was clearest in the IPI 2-3 subgroup, which is precisely her subgroup, with non-inferior overall survival; (3) I am explicitly NOT choosing DA-EPOCH-R (no MYC/BCL2 rearrangement, so no double-hit indication; Alliance showed no survival advantage over R-CHOP in high-risk non-double-hit DLBCL, and it would deliver the same 300 mg/m2 of doxorubicin with more myelosuppression and neuropathy) and NOT R-CODOX-M/R-IVAC (adds 200 mg/m2 more doxorubicin with no survival advantage in DLBCL and excessive toxicity), and NOT dose-dense R-CHOP-14 (no proven benefit); (4) NO UPFRONT consolidation autologous transplant - her disease is not double-hit, the benefit of upfront ASCT in double-expressor lymphoma without rearrangement is unproven, and her cardiac reserve argues against it; ASCT is reserved for relapse; (5) NO PLANNED RADIOTHERAPY - her largest mass is 7.5 cm (not Lugano bulky), disease is multifocal, and she has had prior chest radiotherapy to the left breast; involved-site RT will be reserved for an isolated residual FDG-avid site after systemic therapy (with biopsy first) or for progressive disease. IMPORTANT CONDITIONAL: if polatuzumab vedotin is not available or not covered, I will give R-CHOP x 6 cycles with pegfilgrastim, with (i) doxorubicin dose reduction and/or cardiology-directed modification if cardiology advises, (ii) echocardiogram with GLS before every other cycle (and a hard stop: hold anthracycline if LVEF falls <45% or if any HF symptom develops, and switch to an anthracycline-sparing regimen such as R-CHP if the EF falls below 40%), and (iii) an ACE inhibitor/ARB added for blood pressure (<130/80) and LV support. Before cycle 1 I will add a cardiology/cardio-oncology opinion on whether the EF decline is partly reversible (it may be substantially hypertension-related - she is only on amlodipine with BPs 146-148/88-90 - in which case standard-dose R-CHOP becomes acceptable), send a baseline ECG, obtain a Deauville score and quantitative burden from the staging PET, and repeat brain MRI. I will also recommend intrathecal methotrexate 12 mg on day 1 of cycles 1-3 for CNS prophylaxis (see cns_risk). Timeline: cycle 1 by ~2026-10-05, last dose ~March 2027, interim PET-CT in December 2026 before cycle 4, end-of-treatment PET-CT 6-8 weeks after the last dose. I will not use dose-dense or high-dose regimens, and no central nervous system-directed systemic therapy is planned.
answer.cns_risk: CNS-IPI = 3, i.e. INTERMEDIATE risk (LDH elevated 1; ECOG 1 = 1; stage III-IV = 1; age 59 = 0; eGFR 85 = 0; albumin 3.8 = 0; extranodal sites <=1 - spleen only = 0). She has no clinical CNS involvement and no FDG-avid CNS disease, but PET is insensitive for intracranial disease and the brain was not imaged with MRI. The high-risk extranodal sites that mandate CNS prophylaxis (brain, CSF, leptomeninges, breast, testes, bone marrow, epidural) are not involved: her disease is in the LEFT AXILLARY NODE, not the breast parenchyma (PET shows no FDG-avid breast lesion and the mammogram is BI-RADS 2), so the 'breast involvement' criterion does not apply; marrow is negative; no testicular, adrenal, epidural or ocular involvement. DECISION: (a) obtain a baseline MRI brain with contrast before treatment - justified because PET cannot exclude intracranial disease, she has two separate malignancies (a new CNS metastasis from her ER-positive breast cancer would be an alternative explanation for any neurologic symptom), and CNS-IPI is intermediate; (b) give CNS prophylaxis with intrathecal methotrexate 12 mg on day 1 of cycles 1, 2 and 3, because intermediate CNS-IPI is compounded here by high tumor burden (7.5 cm, SUVmax 22), LDH ~2x ULN and a non-GCB/ABC subtype. I will state plainly to the patient and to the board that the randomized evidence for intrathecal prophylaxis in DLBCL is weak and that this is a risk-based decision; if she declines, or if marrow counts, platelets or renal function preclude lumbar puncture, I will omit it without compromising the systemic regimen. No high-dose methotrexate is indicated (no CNS disease). If any neurologic, cranial nerve, ocular or seizure symptoms develop: urgent MRI brain, lumbar puncture with CSF flow cytometry, cytology and chemistry including CSF protein, and management as CNS lymphoma; before that lumbar puncture I must send SPEP/immunofixation and serum free light chains, which are not in the record, to exclude a monoclonal gammopathy that would confound CSF interpretation.
answer.response_assessment: Interim PET-CT after 3 cycles, before cycle 4 (approximately December 2026), Lugano/Deauville scored, with comparison to the 2026-09-04 baseline study (I will obtain a formal Deauville score and quantitative disease burden for the baseline, which the staging report did not provide): Deauville 1-3 = complete metabolic response - continue the planned regimen to 6 cycles, no biopsy, and repeat PET at the end of treatment; Deauville 4 = partial metabolic response - continue planned therapy and biopsy any single accessible FDG-avid site if uptake is new, enlarging or atypical, since interim PET-positive lesions are false-positive in a minority of cases (infection, inflammation, postoperative change in the left axilla); Deauville 5 = no response/progression - biopsy to confirm before escalating, then treat as refractory/relapsed disease (salvage immunochemotherapy such as R-DHAP or R-ICE, high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell transplant if chemosensitive, or CAR-T if refractory or after transplant, plus clinical trial referral) and add involved-site RT to any localized progressive site. End-of-treatment PET-CT 6-8 weeks after the last cycle (approximately May 2027): Deauville 1-3 = complete metabolic response and observation; Deauville 4-5 = biopsy any residual FDG-avid lesion before escalating (inflammation/infection must be excluded), consider involved-site radiotherapy for an isolated residual PET-positive lesion and consider autologous transplant in a chemosensitive patient. Interim laboratory monitoring: CBC weekly during neutropenia and CBC/CMP/LDH before every cycle; uric acid, potassium and creatinine with allopurinol in cycles 1-2 for tumor lysis risk (formally low: urate 5.8, normal renal function, no kidney involvement) and hydration; track temperature log, weight, B symptoms and ECOG at every visit; repeat echocardiogram with GLS every 2 cycles and after the final cycle. No repeat bone marrow biopsy is needed (marrow negative at diagnosis). Surveillance after complete response: history, examination and CBC every 3 months for 2 years then every 6 months to year 5, with PET-CT at 6-12 months and then annually as clinically indicated, and continued annual mammography/breast surveillance for her prior breast cancer.
answer.pretreatment_workup: COMPLETED AND ADEQUATE: CBC with differential 2026-09-01 (WBC 6.9, ANC 4.6, Hgb 11.4, platelets 178); CMP 2026-09-01 (Cr 0.8, eGFR 85, Na 139, K 4.2, Cl 103, CO2 25, BUN 14, glucose 96, Ca 9.3, albumin 3.8, total protein 7.0, AST 24, ALT 22, ALP 92, total bilirubin 0.6, phosphate 3.6); LDH 510 (elevated, versus 182 in March 2026); urate 5.8; beta-2 microglobulin 2.9; viral serologies 2026-09-01 - HBsAg, total anti-HBc, anti-HBs, HCV Ab and HIV-1/2 Ag/Ab all non-reactive (so no antiviral prophylaxis is required, but she is hepatitis B non-immune and should be vaccinated); staging FDG PET-CT skull base to mid-thigh 2026-09-04 with no FDG-avid disease in liver, adrenals, kidneys, lungs, bone, marrow or breasts and physiologic brain uptake only; bone marrow aspirate and core biopsy 2026-09-08 negative for lymphoma; diagnostic excisional biopsy with full IHC, flow and FISH (amended 2026-09-08); baseline transthoracic echocardiogram with strain 2026-09-09 (LVEF 45% biplane, mild global hypokinesis, GLS -14%, grade I diastolic dysfunction, mild MR, normal RV with TAPSE 2.1 cm, RVSP 28 mmHg, no effusion; comparison LVEF 62% in 2016). OUTSTANDING BEFORE CYCLE 1: 12-lead ECG with QTc and rhythm; formal Deauville score and quantitative disease burden (sum of product of diameters) from the staging PET-CT via nuclear medicine; MRI brain with contrast; cardiology/cardio-oncology consultation with an explicit surveillance plan (echo with GLS every 2 cycles, MUGA if echo is not reproducible), baseline NT-proBNP and hs-troponin, and a blood-pressure/ACEi-ARB optimization plan; SPEP with immunofixation and serum free light chains (needed before any lumbar puncture, and to exclude a coexisting monoclonal gammopathy); ophthalmologic examination if any ocular symptoms (or as a baseline given ABC subtype); dental clearance before chemotherapy; DEXA (last 2025, lumbar T-score -1.8) and a zoledronic acid plan for AI- and chemotherapy-related bone loss; inactivated influenza, COVID-19 and pneumococcal vaccination, plus hepatitis B vaccination (anti-HBs negative); documentation of menopausal status, fertility considerations and contraception (chemotherapy teratogenicity; not practically relevant at 59); confirm no active infection - repeat CBC, review the fevers (she has taken acetaminophen, which can mask a low-grade infection), and assess TB risk before steroids; baseline weights and ECOG for response and toxicity tracking; germline counseling consideration given two primary malignancies at age 59 (no BRCA testing has ever been done, criteria were not met in 2016); anticoagulation and NSAID-avoidance plan if intrathecal methotrexate is used; and documentation of prior left breast radiation dosimetry/heart dose, which is not in the record and would refine her cardiac risk.
answer.supportive_care: Neutropenia: pegfilgrastim 6 mg SC on day 9 of every cycle (mandatory with polatuzumab/R-CHP in POLARIX; also indicated by her age, IPI and prior cytotoxic therapy) with weekly CBC; filgrastim 300-468 mcg daily from day 9 to 14 is an acceptable alternative if she prefers a shorter needle. Infection prophylaxis: TMP-SMX double-strength 1 tablet daily (or 3x weekly) from day 14 of cycle 1 through 6 months after the last dose of chemotherapy, with atovaquone 1500 mg daily substituted if she develops intolerance - her allergy is to penicillin (hives) and sulfonamide allergy does not cross-react with penicillin, so TMP-SMX is appropriate. Acyclovir 400 mg PO twice daily during the 5-day prednisone pulses (and for any prolonged steroid course or severe mucositis); fluconazole 100 mg daily only if mucositis develops or steroids are extended beyond the pulses. Rituximab premedication with acetaminophen 650 mg plus cetirizine 10 mg (+/- naloxone), slow initial infusion rate with 1-hour observation, and steroids plus rate reduction if she has a grade 3 or 4 infusion reaction (late reactions can occur); polatuzumab premedication with corticosteroid, acetaminophen and antihistamine, and proactive antiemetics (ondansetron 8-16 mg with dexamethasone) because nausea is frequent; monitor for polatuzumab peripheral neuropathy (sensory, mostly grade 1-2 - dose reduce and treat with gabapentin/duloxetine if needed, and warn her that this could temporarily affect fine work skills) and for the rare infusion reaction and rare pneumonitis/ILD (new cough or dyspnea requires urgent evaluation and drug withdrawal). Other: avoid NSAIDs (renal and tumor lysis risk); acetaminophen up to 3 g/day for fevers and night sweats with a continued temperature log; no aspirin; no intramuscular injections and check platelets before each intrathecal dose; allopurinol 100-300 mg daily for cycles 1-2 with 2-3 L/day oral hydration; monitor glucose during prednisone pulses (glucose 96, no diabetes); monitor sodium and potassium with polyuria. Bone health: zoledronic acid 5 mg IV (or denosumab 60 mg SC every 6 months) every 3-6 months with calcium 1000-1200 mg/day and vitamin D 800-1000 IU/day (she is already on calcium/vitamin D), DEXA after completion of anastrozole, and dental clearance - she has osteopenia (T-score -1.8) plus planned repeated prednisone exposure. Anastrozole: CONTINUE to complete her planned 10-year course in November 2026 - there is no interaction with polatuzumab/R-CHP, she has only ~2-3 months remaining, and she is osteopenic so the bone protection is worth more than a trivial reduction in breast cancer risk; she should NOT extend beyond 10 years without breast oncology review. Vaccines: inactivated influenza, COVID-19 and pneumococcal vaccine early in therapy; no live vaccines during treatment and for at least 6-12 months after (also advise household contacts to avoid live vaccines such as rotavirus/oral polio). Bone marrow and fertility: pregnancy must be avoided during and for 6 months after therapy (formalistic at 59, postmenopausal). Supportive non-pharmacologic: graded aerobic and resistance exercise (she normally takes 3 exercise classes weekly and has stopped) cleared by cardiology given EF 45%; nutrition counseling to reverse her 3.7% weight loss and maintain protein/calorie intake; psycho-oncology referral, a lymphoma survivor/support group, and body-image counselling for expected alopecia (no scalp cooling with rituximab- or polatuzumab-containing regimens because of alopecia risk and infusion reactions); her husband is her primary driver and caregiver, so he should be included in education and in the fever/neuro-symptom action plan; she should be instructed to report any temperature >=38.0 C, and any rash, dyspnea, cough, neuropathy, confusion, headache, weakness or bowel/bladder change immediately.
answer.fitness_and_goals: She is fit for curative-intensity therapy: ECOG 1, independent in all activities, still working her usual full-time hours as a school librarian, climbs two flights of stairs without stopping, NYHA class I, no dyspnea/orthopnea/edema/chest pain/palpitations/syncope, no neurologic symptoms, and no diabetes, cirrhosis, HIV or other active comorbidity; renal and hepatic function are normal and marrow reserve is adequate. The one fitness limitation is cardiopulmonary reserve: LVEF 45% with GLS -14% and grade I diastolic dysfunction after 240 mg/m2 doxorubicin and left breast radiotherapy, currently untreated for her suboptimally controlled hypertension (138-148/88-90 on amlodipine alone) - this is the single issue that must be addressed before and during treatment, and it is a chronic, partly modifiable risk rather than an acute contraindication. GOALS (documented at the 2026-09-17 visit, and to be confirmed with her and her husband): she wants treatment aimed at cure and hopes to return to full-time work at the school library; she is explicitly worried about her heart given her mother's heart failure and asked whether the echo finding affects her treatment and whether she should keep taking anastrozole. My answers to her: her reduced EF is a late effect of her 2016 anthracycline and chest radiotherapy (plus hypertension), is not caused by the lymphoma, does not change the need for curative treatment, and is precisely why I am omitting doxorubicin and adding blood-pressure and LV-protective therapy with serial echocardiographic surveillance; and she should keep taking anastrozole to November 2026 with bone protection. Practical implications I will commit to: treatment on a 21-day cycle with a single long infusion day per cycle (roughly 4-5 months of therapy), the expectation of returning to work between cycles with a 2-4 week recovery after each cycle, a realistic discussion that fatigue and neuropathy will be most pronounced in weeks 2-3 of each cycle, and an explicit plan for occupational support (alternative duties, reduced hours during fatigue) and cardiac rehabilitation. I will document an advance-care discussion only as a routine part of curative-intent consent, and I will revisit her goals explicitly after the interim PET-CT.
missing_information: No 12-lead ECG (rhythm, QTc) documented before planned chemotherapy - required baseline for anthracycline-class and rituximab therapy and for arrhythmia risk.

No cardiology/cardio-oncology consultation or documented surveillance plan; no NT-proBNP or hs-troponin; no MUGA; no baseline strain comparator (2016 study did not perform GLS), so the LVEF fall from 62% to 45% cannot be confidently attributed to anthracycline versus hypertension versus occult cardiomyopathy; no prior radiation dosimetry/heart dose from the 2016 left breast tangents is recorded.

No upper limit of normal for LDH is provided, so the LDH ratio (used in IPI and CNS-IPI) cannot be computed exactly; only a single post-diagnosis LDH value (510) exists with no recent trend (prior 182 in March 2026).

No formal Deauville score and no quantitative disease burden (sum of product of diameters) for the staging PET-CT - the report is descriptive only, and a scored baseline is required for interim comparison.
No MRI brain; PET is insensitive for intracranial disease and there is no baseline imaging to exclude occult CNS involvement.
No ophthalmologic examination documented; no assessment for ocular/vitreoretinal involvement despite a non-GCB (ABC) subtype.
No SPEP/immunofixation and no serum free light chains - needed before any lumbar puncture or CSF assessment and to exclude a coexisting monoclonal gammopathy.

No conventional karyotype/cytogenetics result reported although tissue was submitted for cytogenetics; no MYC H-score or formal double-expressor classification per WHO-HAEM5; no centralized/expert hematopathology review of the 2026-08-25 biopsy to confirm DLBCL, NOS versus a specific molecular subtype.

No baseline record of menopausal status, contraceptive/tertiary fertility counselling, or pregnancy testing; no documentation of whether she is fully vaccinated (influenza/COVID-19/pneumococcal) or that hepatitis B vaccination has been arranged (she is anti-HBs negative).
No dental clearance documented before chemotherapy; DEXA is from 2025 (lumbar T-score -1.8) and no 2026 DEXA or zoledronic acid plan is recorded.
No documentation of blood-pressure optimization (on amlodipine only, BPs 146-148/88-90) or of whether an ACE inhibitor/ARB has been considered, and no cardiology recommendation on doxorubicin dosing.
No germline risk assessment/counselling despite two primary cancers in a decade (no BRCA testing ever performed; 2016 criteria not met); no documentation of the genetic counseling discussion.

No baseline assessment excluding an infectious cause of the fevers beyond clinical description (no repeat CBC, CRP, blood cultures; no review of TB/fungal risk before corticosteroid therapy); acetaminophen use may have masked low-grade infection.
No record of a documented treatment start date or regimen schedule, and no consent/education record for polatuzumab-related neuropathy, infusion reactions or the cardiac monitoring plan.

No documentation of baseline performance-status/weight trend beyond the recorded weights, and no baseline audiometry (relevant if any ototoxic regimen is later considered) or baseline oral/dental assessment.

items.criterion: The response states the diagnosis is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (NOS) with a non-germinal-center (non-GCB) phenotype by the Hans algorithm.
The response notes that Hans non-GCB is an immunohistochemical surrogate and is not equivalent to molecular ABC cell-of-origin by gene-expression profiling.
The response states the left axillary node is lymphoma and not recurrent breast carcinoma (cytokeratin AE1/AE3 and GATA3 negative).
The response stages the disease as Lugano/Ann Arbor stage III (nodes on both sides of the diaphragm with splenic involvement).
The response explains that the spleen is lymphatic tissue (a nodal site), so splenic nodules do not make the disease stage IV, and that there is no non-lymphatic extranodal or marrow involvement.
The response notes B symptoms (documented fevers >38 C and drenching night sweats).
The response notes the 7.5 cm mass is below the 10 cm Lugano bulk threshold, acknowledging that bulk definitions vary (some trials use 7.5 cm).
The response stages this patient as stage IV (e.g. by counting splenic involvement as extranodal disease).
The response classifies the lymphoma as double-expressor by IHC (MYC 45% >=40%, BCL2 70% >=50%) but NOT double-hit (FISH shows no MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement).
The response classifies this lymphoma as double-hit / high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements.
The response recommends DA-EPOCH-R (or another intensified regimen) on the basis of double-expressor biology.
The response calculates IPI as 2 (low-intermediate risk): elevated LDH and stage III; age 59, ECOG 1 and no extranodal sites (spleen is not counted as extranodal) score zero.
The response calculates CNS-IPI as 2 (intermediate risk).
The response states that routine CNS prophylaxis is not indicated (CNS-IPI 2, no kidney/adrenal, testicular or breast involvement).
The response mandates CNS prophylaxis (high-dose methotrexate or intrathecal therapy) for this patient.

The response recognizes anthracycline-related cardiac risk (prior doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left chest radiotherapy, LVEF fall from 62% to 45%, i.e. cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction) and does NOT plan standard full-dose doxorubicin (R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP) without first addressing cardiac function.

The response recommends standard R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP (full-dose doxorubicin) without conditioning it on the reduced LVEF / prior anthracycline exposure (e.g. without cardio-oncology clearance, a cardioprotective modification, or a non-anthracycline alternative).
The response requests urgent cardio-oncology (or cardiology) evaluation before starting therapy.
The response starts or optimizes guideline-directed cardioprotective therapy: an ACE inhibitor/ARB (or ARNI) plus a beta-blocker (e.g. carvedilol), for example replacing amlodipine.

The response recommends a curative-intent anthracycline-free or anthracycline-modified regimen, e.g. R-CEOP (etoposide in place of doxorubicin) or R-GCVP; R-CHOP with liposomal doxorubicin or dexrazoxane is acceptable only if conditioned on cardio-oncology judging it safe.
The response acknowledges that anthracycline-free regimens likely have lower efficacy than anthracycline-based therapy.
The response plans serial cardiac monitoring during therapy: repeat LVEF/GLS imaging plus troponin and/or natriuretic peptide (BNP/NT-proBNP).
The response recommends palliative-only treatment, best supportive care, or hospice as the plan.
The response plans an end-of-treatment FDG PET-CT read with Lugano criteria / Deauville 5-point scale.
The response assesses tumor lysis risk as low-intermediate (normal creatinine and uric acid, LDH ~2x ULN) and gives allopurinol with hydration for cycle 1.
The response recommends (or reasonably considers) primary G-CSF support with each cycle.
The response addresses the ongoing anastrozole: continuing it is acceptable (no meaningful interaction), or holding it in coordination with breast oncology is also acceptable.
The response confirms hepatitis B serology was checked (HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive) before rituximab.
The response judges the patient fit for curative-intent therapy (ECOG 1, normal organ function apart from the LVEF) and acknowledges her goal of cure.
The response lists the cause of the LVEF decline / cardio-oncology work-up as missing (e.g. ischemic evaluation given prior left chest radiotherapy, cardiac MRI, baseline troponin and NT-proBNP).
